note: NWPP KEEPER #4, PROMOTED 2026-09-22 (lane NWPP-46) BY OWNER RULING, verbatim: "Is this a recommended keeper candidate? If so plz promote. If structural integrity improves but gates regress that may still be a keeper." THIS PROMOTION IS ON THE EASY LIMB: NO GATE REGRESSES. The gate profile is IDENTICAL to the predecessor -- C1 FAIL, C2 PASS, C4 FAIL, C6 PASS, C8 PASS, determination NOT-YET on {fuelmix, dispatch_corr} -- and NO C1 row changed status. *** THE LANE RE-DIAGNOSED ITS OWN CHARTER, ON MEASUREMENT, AND THE RE-DIAGNOSIS IS THE MAIN RESULT. *** NWPP-46 was chartered to close C4 coal on the COAL OFFER STACK's vertical extent (NWPP-43 section 4.1, carried by NWPP-44/45). NWPP's OWN DATA FALSIFIES THAT PREMISE TWICE, both zero-LP. (1) THE '$0.51/MWh SHELF' IS A FLEET MIX ARTIFACT, NOT A WITHIN-PLANT SLOPE. Rebuilding the keeper fleet through the sanctioned replay_keeper path (run_year(fleet_only=True), scripts/probes/_nwpp46_coal_stack_phase0.py) shows econlo == econhi == peak EXACTLY, to the cent, at ALL 17 NWPP coal plants. The $0.51 is the difference between FLEET AVERAGES over different plant mixes. Cause: pipeline/backcast_config.py:2372 deep-merges _SPP_OFFER_CURVE, whose _SPP_COAL_IDENTITY_BANDS are 1.0 on EVERY band, for iso in ('SPP','NWPP') -- a posture declared by lane NWPP-20 before any NWPP solve existed, to avoid transplanting ERCOT's fitted bands under rule 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE], while GENERIC_BASE_OFFER_CURVE['COAL_BIT'] is itself sloped (econ_low 0.95 / econ_high 1.10 / peak 1.45). (2) THE CORRECT LADDER IS SMALL AND WOULD BE INERT ANYWAY. Reproducing the shared WP-3 construction of scripts/data/derive_campd_marginal_hr.py BAND FOR BAND over 511,855 steady-state coal unit-hours from NWPP's own CEMS 2023-2025 gives cap-weighted marg_committed 0.821 / marg_econ_low 0.932 / marg_econ_high 1.004 / marg_peak 1.029, i.e. econ_high/econ_low = 1.077 (p25 1.052 / p50 1.082 / p75 1.123; 17 of 24 units above 1.05) -- a 7.7% rise across the economic range, 10.4% across the whole dispatchable range, about $3/MWh on a $35 offer, NOT the 0.9-1.7 GW of missing diurnal swing. AND IT COULD NOT BITE: NWPP-INLAND / NWPP-NW / NWPP-OR each carry exactly TWELVE distinct P1 prices for the WHOLE YEAR -- one per month, median 1 per day, mean within-day swing $0.00 (NWPP-EAST 84/187/218 prices, $1.74-4.06). A coal plant facing a within-month-constant price runs flat-out or not at all for the month whatever ladder its offer carries. WHAT C4 ACTUALLY IS: HYDRO OVER-FLEXIBILITY. The marginal unit in those zones is hydro and its monthly-budget dual is a month-constant water value. Measured against the SAME EIA-930 series the scorer uses: model hydro runs 114/120/138% of the real diurnal swing while coal runs 10/5/4% and gas 65-69%; solar and wind match at ratio 1.00, so it is not a renewables artifact, and hydro's MEAN LEVEL is right (12.200/12.315/12.908 GW vs 11.899/11.991/12.588). On the additive h19-h11 evening-ramp metric hydro's EXCESS accounts for 69/87/102% of the coal+gas ramp deficit. The ratio WORSENS year on year (1.14 -> 1.38) exactly as real hydro flexibility falls (5.511 -> 4.477 GW) while the model's stays pinned near 6.2 -- with coal's ratio worsening 0.10 -> 0.04 in lockstep. Two sides of one object. Lever (C) was closed for free on the committed diagnostics: D-2 reads COAL forced_twh = 0.0 in all three years and D-4 carries no coal row, so there is NO coal floor to be binding off-window. THE ARM: hydro_dispatch_envelope (caiso-72) + hydro_min_flow_floor (caiso-124), NWPP, backcast. ONE MECHANISM, TWO MIRRORED HALVES, NEVER ARMED APART -- constants.py defines HYDRO_MIN_FLOW_PERCENTILE = 100.0 - HYDRO_ENVELOPE_PERCENTILE, so the two-sided envelope is identified by the ONE percentile the ceiling already carries; read as an exceedance level the floor is Q95, the hydrological low-flow index environmental / FERC minimum-flow licence conditions are themselves written against. ZERO new free parameters (rule 21 [R-DOF]: build_dof_ledger emits 4 entries / 3 residual, IDENTICAL to NWPP-40/41/42/44) and ZERO code change (rule 24: both are existing ScenarioConfig fields reached from the calibration CLI; src/ is UNTOUCHED by this lane). RULE 25 [R-ISO-SCOPE]: NOTHING IS TRANSFERRED FROM CAISO -- ceiling and floor are built from NWPP's OWN EIA-930 NG:WAT meter; the percentile is the shared structural convention in constants.py. MEASURED BINDING, AND THE TWO HALVES ARE DISJOINT. Ceiling: 21.7/23.7/23.4% of hours, 1.864/2.359/2.684 TWh above, concentrated h16-h22 (29-47% of those hours) -- the perfect-foresight hoarding an energy-only budget cap permits. Floor: 10.4/12.9/14.0% of hours, 0.866/1.185/1.526 TWh below, concentrated in the MIDDAY SOLAR BELLY and the OVERNIGHT SHOULDER. Disjoint hours is the rule 19 [R-ONE-MECH] evidence that they are one reconciled family and not a stack. RULE 17 [R-FLOOR-WINDOW] for the floor half: (a) driver = run-of-river inflow that cannot be stored plus the licence minimum releases the energy-only budget ignores; (b) window = all 24 h, and D-4 scores off-window share 0.0 in EVERY year; (c) forward story = re-derives from the pooled HYDRO_CLIMATOLOGY_YEARS percentile and responds to the water year through the budget it is clipped against. THE PRE-REGISTERED KILL CONDITION WAS CODED AND COMMITTED BEFORE THE FIRST LEG LANDED (scripts/probes/_nwpp46_gates.py at 9cd108d9), deliberately, so it could not be written to fit the numbers; it SELF-TESTS against the predecessor, where it correctly reads I. It does NOT fire in either direction. INERT limb: the hydro amplitude ratio had to fall >= 0.03 in EVERY year (2023 < 1.11, 2024 < 1.17, 2025 < 1.35); it reads 1.048 / 1.107 / 1.148 against 1.138 / 1.200 / 1.383. OVERSHOOT (a): below 0.90 in any year; the minimum is 1.048. OVERSHOOT (b): any C1 COAL row outside +/-8.00 TWh; every coal row is inside (max |delta| 6.59, 2025 COAL_BIT). OVERSHOOT (c): hydro annual energy moving > 5.0 TWh; it moved 0.000 TWh in every year. THE EX-ANTE PREDICTION LANDED. PRECOMMIT section 6a predicted the hydro amplitude ratio at 1.05 / 1.10 / 1.16 from a static clip of the predecessor's own hourly hydro; the SOLVE returned 1.048 / 1.107 / 1.148, within 0.002 / 0.007 / 0.012. Section 6d predicted C4 r at 0.61-0.66 / 0.60-0.65 / 0.62-0.67 and NRMSE at 0.24-0.28 / 0.23-0.27 / 0.26-0.30; the solve returned r 0.658 / 0.617 / 0.637 and NRMSE 0.244 / 0.240 / 0.276 -- every value INSIDE its pre-registered band. WHAT IMPROVES. C4 coal improves on BOTH metrics in ALL THREE years: r 0.605/0.595/0.610 -> 0.658/0.617/0.637 and NRMSE 0.260/0.246/0.284 -> 0.244/0.240/0.276. The mechanism's own signature moved as claimed: coal's diurnal amplitude ratio 0.100/0.052/0.037 -> 0.223/0.096/0.089, i.e. its peak-to-trough swing roughly DOUBLED in every year (0.090->0.199, 0.068->0.126, 0.063->0.151 GW). D-1 corroborates from a second instrument: coal's off-peak CV ratio roughly doubled-to-quadrupled (COAL_BIT 0.147->0.265, 0.041->0.090, 0.022->0.097; COAL_PRB 0.074->0.115, 0.067->0.124, 0.044->0.076). WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, STATED AT THE GATE AND NOT ABSORBED. C4 STILL FAILS -- r remains below the 0.70 floor in all three years, EXACTLY as the PRECOMMIT predicted, and it is reported as a FAIL, not a near-miss. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT]: C4 was never the reason to arm this and is not a promotion criterion in either direction; a head/flow deliverability ceiling and a licence minimum-flow release are real features of how this fleet operates. THE INTRA-DAY TERM DOES NOT UNIFORMLY IMPROVE: r_intra rises sharply in 2023 (0.218 -> 0.371) but is FLAT in 2024 (0.376 -> 0.375) and WORSE in 2025 (0.425 -> 0.374); 2024/2025's r gain comes mostly from the daily-mean term (0.664->0.679, 0.715->0.732) and from amplitude. Getting the SIZE of the swing right is not the same as getting its HOUR right, and this arm did the first more than the second. ONE D-1 LEG MOVES THE WRONG WAY: 2023 COAL_BIT profile r 0.756 -> 0.723 and 2023 COAL_WC (a 0.4 TWh class) -0.072 -> -0.583, while 2023 COAL_PRB moves the other way 0.505 -> 0.779. The price is STILL near-monthly in the hydro-set zones: the p95 ceiling is GENEROUS (the measured fleet reaches p95 only 5% of the time while the model may sit there always), so even clipped, hydro still over-swings at 1.05-1.15x. The coal offer stack is STILL THE IDENTITY, and the measured ladder above is ROUTED for after the price acquires intra-day variation, not dismissed. ONE EX-ANTE PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND IS REPORTED AS SUCH. PRECOMMIT section 6e predicted 2023 CC_REGULAR -- the SINGLE failing C1 row -- would IMPROVE; it moved 0.422 TWh FURTHER OUT (-8.219 -> -8.641), and 2024/2025 moved out too (-6.323 -> -6.790, -4.714 -> -5.442). The reasoning that failed is recorded so it is not repeated: the PRECOMMIT argued the hydro budget's upper bound is a CAP, not an equality, so water refused in the evening need not all be re-placed and the marginal class would absorb the difference. In the event the FLOOR half pushed hydro UP in the trough by exactly what the ceiling clipped from the evening, so hydro annual energy moved 0.000 TWh and there was no released VOLUME for CC_REGULAR to pick up -- only a reshaped one, which CT_PEAKER and coal took a share of. C1's single failing row is therefore still 2023 CC_REGULAR and it is marginally worse in magnitude while unchanged in verdict. C8 IS NOT AT RISK AND DID NOT MOVE. MECH_HYDRO_MIN_FLOW is classed NON-THERMAL forcing (water, not a commitment decision), so D-2 REPORTS it -- 52.989/55.847/57.754 TWh, 49.6/51.8/51.1% of hydro, against CAISO's own measured 36-46% -- but EXCLUDES it from the merchant thermal forced-share arithmetic; C8 reads PASS with forced_share 0.0 on every gated thermal class. HOW IT WAS SOLVED. Three YEAR-ISOLATED shards (rule 36 [R-YEAR-ISOLATION]) pinned to the immutable SHA 87201a18bae068f0accbf0e17d9e5fa3911f4ac3, each pushing its FULL bundle including dispatch/<year>_P1.parquet (rule 34(a)); the parent ran ZERO LP (rule 32(a)). Each shard ran scripts/replay_keeper.py --set against the PREDECESSOR's own meta.json rather than a hand-built CLI -- deliberately, because meta.json is what carries hydro_backfill_year=2024, the loader kwarg whose omission silently invalidated NWPP-44's entire first shard wave. G-DRIFT (rule 29(b) form 4) WAS ESTABLISHED MECHANICALLY, NOT BY HUNK-READING. 29 files changed on the solve path since the predecessor's git_sha ee276d87 (5,983 insertions). Rather than classify them by hand, the lane created a git worktree at ee276d87, rebuilt the predecessor's own recipe on BOTH trees, and diffed the LP INPUT ARRAYS: unit_ids IDENTICAL (646 / 642 rows), and mc (646 x 8760), pmax, pmin, heat_rate, vom, availability and demand all max|delta| = 0 in 2023 and 2025. Every LP input is bit-identical across the drift, which covers all 29 files on the input path at once. The remaining surface was classified by hunk: rows.py is a pure _add_bounds accumulator refactor, model.py/lp/__init__.py add full_extract which skips P0 diagnostic extraction only, and solve.py un-nests the same-year P1 basis seed -- the one hunk worth naming -- but resolve_p1_basis_seed_default still defaults OFF and replay_keeper pins it to 0 regardless.
